interpretation: Sudachi satisfied all requested morphology capabilities for every case.
GiNZA output remained partial because coreference_candidate was not fulfilled; assurance therefore never passed even for the aligned case.
Fulfilled dependency and scope capabilities remained usable as candidate material despite the partial provider state.
Dependency projection exposed an independent acts_on conflict in the multiple-action cases; resolving one condition attachment did not erase that conflict.
Shared domain vocabulary and an opposing result action no longer produced a false pass in these cases.
limitations: These are engineered local smoke cases, not an accuracy, recall, precision, or field-value evaluation.
The observations do not establish general dependency, scope, coordination, coreference, or cross-sentence quality.
Provider identity and resource versions are locally reported, not cryptographically attested.
The workflow result is not human acceptance or proof that an agent action occurred.
